9: My design is intended to describe a distribution, amount, frequency, or proportion rather than isolate a causal effect.
I have stated what the descriptive evidence can and cannot represent.
I have not invented an intervention simply to make the study seem more scientific.
10: Every variable being described has an operational definition.
I know what one independent observational case/unit represents.
I have not added IV/DV or hypothesis language unless my actual question requires it.
11: I distinguished the target population/system from the actual sample.
My measurement procedure produces the variable I claim to describe.
I stated the boundary on generalization and reviewed ethics/safety.
12: Another person could reproduce the descriptive collection procedure.
I know exactly what one row and each column mean.
Missing and exclusion rules are recorded before final analysis.
13: The distribution/counts/proportions were inspected before interpretation.
Descriptive summaries match the data type.
14: I named the descriptive quantity or estimand that answers the question.
The analysis is no more complex than the question requires.
Any inferential extension is justified by sampling/design rather than added automatically.
15: The Results report the observed distribution/count/proportion/summary clearly.
Every result is traceable to the data or analysis record.
The wording remains descriptive and does not imply causation.
16: The Discussion answers the descriptive question directly.
Interpretations stay within the studied sample/system and measurement.
Limitations explain what cannot be generalized or inferred.

9: The key predictor/exposure is measured, not assigned by the researcher.
The design can estimate association/difference/prediction without claiming direct causation.
My claim boundary explicitly acknowledges observational limitations.
10: The measured predictor/exposure and outcome are both operationally defined.
I identified plausible confounders or alternative explanations.
11: Sampling and measurement support the association I want to estimate.
I stated how sampling limits generalization.
Ethics, privacy, and measurement quality are addressed before collection.
12: The protocol preserves IDs, pairing, clustering, or repeated structure where relevant.
The planned analysis matches the observational question.
13: I inspected distributions and the predictor–outcome relationship before inference.
The raw data and corrections are traceable.
Repeated or clustered observations remain identifiable.
14: The estimand states the association/difference I actually want to estimate.
The analysis matches outcome type, pairing/clustering, and design.
Magnitude and uncertainty are planned alongside any p-value.
15: Results report association/difference without causal wording.
Key estimates and uncertainty are traceable to stored output.
Null or weak findings are reported transparently.
16: The direct answer uses observational language.
Alternative explanations, confounding, or reverse direction are considered.
Limitations keep causal and generalization claims bounded.

9: The key condition is deliberately manipulated or assigned.
I stated the causal claim boundary before seeing results.
10: The manipulated factor and measured outcome are operationally defined.
I know the experimental unit that independently receives treatment.
Control/comparison and controlled procedures are distinguished.
11: Sampling/generalization and measurement quality are explicit.
The experiment is safe and permitted before collection.
The measurement genuinely represents the intended outcome.
12: Replication is counted at the experimental-unit level.
The protocol and analysis preserve the actual treatment structure.
13: Raw data remain unchanged and unit/treatment IDs are preserved.
I inspected treatment-group distributions and unusual observations.
14: The estimand is the treatment contrast of interest.
The analysis matches treatment structure, experimental unit, and outcome type.
Effect magnitude and uncertainty will be reported.
15: Results report the treatment contrast and exact supporting output.
Statistical significance is not treated as effect magnitude.
Mechanistic explanations remain for Discussion unless directly measured.
16: The Discussion separates observed treatment effects from proposed mechanisms.
Internal-validity and implementation limitations are considered.
Generalization is limited to supported populations/conditions.

9: An intervention/condition exists, but assignment is not fully randomized.
I have identified what makes the design quasi-experimental.
The causal claim boundary reflects selection/confounding threats.
10: Intervention/exposure, outcome, units, and comparison structure are defined.
I am not treating nonrandom groups as automatically equivalent.
11: Sampling and measurement quality are documented.
Baseline/group differences that affect interpretation are considered.
Ethics and intervention authority are resolved before collection.
12: Timing, fidelity, comparison procedures, unit IDs, and planned adjustment/analysis are documented.
The protocol records how nonrandom assignment will be handled analytically and interpretively.
Missing/exclusion rules are prespecified where possible.
13: I inspected baseline differences, missingness, implementation, and outcome distributions.
Raw data and protocol deviations are preserved.
Group membership and repeated structure remain traceable.
14: The analysis estimates the intended comparison without pretending adjustment creates randomization.
Relevant baseline variables/design structure are considered.
Magnitude and uncertainty are reported with the quasi-experimental boundary.
15: Results report the adjusted/unadjusted comparison exactly as analyzed.
The Results do not claim randomization that did not occur.
Weak or contradictory findings are reported.
16: The Discussion addresses selection/confounding threats directly.
Causal wording is calibrated to the actual quasi-experimental design.
Limitations explain how nonrandom assignment restricts interpretation.

9: The design matches a question about meaning, experience, process, explanation, or context.
I stated what kind of qualitative evidence will answer the question.
My claim boundary is contextual and does not promise statistical population causation.
10: The central phenomenon/domains are defined without forcing them into IV/DV language.
I know what participant, case, document, observation, or excerpt supplies evidence.
I have stated what will count as relevant evidence.
11: The sampling/recruitment strategy fits the qualitative purpose.
The interview/observation/document procedure is clear and credible.
Ethics, privacy, reflexivity, and transferability boundaries are addressed.
12: The collection protocol and qualitative corpus structure are auditable.
The coding/category/theme plan and trustworthiness protections are documented.
I have rules for missing, withdrawn, excluded, or unusable evidence.
13: The original qualitative corpus is preserved.
I summarized the corpus and inspected patterns before final themes were fixed.
14: The analysis explains how codes/categories/themes or interpretations will be developed.
I documented credibility checks such as audit trail, discrepant evidence, coding consistency, or reflexivity as relevant.
I am not adding a p-value or effect-size requirement that the qualitative question does not need.
15: Each major finding/theme is traceable to qualitative evidence.
The Results distinguish participant evidence from my interpretation.
Variation, contradictory/disconfirming evidence, or boundary cases are reported when relevant.
16: The Discussion answers the qualitative question in context.
Alternative interpretations and researcher/context effects are considered.
Transferability and other limitations are described without pretending statistical generalization.

9: The review design matches a question answered from existing research.
I stated the scope/type of synthesis.
My claim boundary depends on search coverage, included studies, and evidence quality.
10: Review concepts, populations/contexts, outcomes/phenomena, and unit of inclusion are defined.
I am not inventing IV/DV or participant terminology that the review does not need.
Eligibility concepts can be applied consistently during screening.
11: The target literature and search/screening strategy are clear.
Coverage limits are stated before making a global gap claim.
12: Search, deduplication, screening, extraction, and synthesis procedures are auditable.
One study-matrix row/unit and all key extraction columns are defined.
Missing/unreported study information and exclusion decisions have explicit rules.
13: The master source/extraction record is preserved.
Included-study scope and characteristics are summarized.
Screening/extraction corrections and decision changes are traceable.
14: The synthesis approach matches the review question.
Comparability, study design, measurement, context, and evidence-quality differences are examined.
I am not forcing a statistical test or pooled effect into a narrative review.
15: Results report the number/scope of included studies and the evidence synthesis.
Theme or evidence claims are traceable to included studies.
No pooled effect is invented from incomparable studies.
16: The Discussion/conclusion answers the review question from the included evidence.
Coverage and study-quality limitations constrain the claims.
Any research-gap statement stays bounded by the documented search.

9: The question requires quantitative synthesis of existing comparable effects.
I stated the scope of studies/effects and claim boundary.
I understand that meta-analysis still depends on study quality and comparability.
10: Treatment/exposure, outcome/effect metric, eligibility concepts, and independent effect unit are defined.
Multiple effects from the same sample will not automatically be treated as independent.
The effect definition matches the review question.
11: Search, screening, extraction, and appraisal procedures are planned.
Coverage/generalization limits of the included literature are explicit.
Effect-size information can be obtained or converted consistently.
12: Effect extraction/conversion and dependence rules are prespecified.
One effect-size row and all variance/SE/study-ID fields are defined.
Missing-statistic and duplicate-sample decisions are documented.
13: Extracted effects and study characteristics are checked before pooling.
Corrections and conversions are traceable to source reports.
14: The pooled estimand/effect metric and model are defined.
Heterogeneity, dependence, sensitivity, and moderator decisions are justified.
Pooled magnitude and uncertainty are central; p-values are secondary.
15: Results report pooled estimate, uncertainty, study count/effect count, and heterogeneity where appropriate.
Forest/other outputs are traceable to extracted effects.
Sensitivity or conflicting evidence is reported transparently.
16: Interpretation accounts for heterogeneity, bias, study quality, and dependence.
The pooled estimate is not generalized beyond represented populations/outcomes/designs.
Limitations distinguish meta-analytic model limits from primary-study limits.

9: I can explain why one evidence type alone is insufficient.
The quantitative and qualitative strands each answer a defined part of the question.
I stated how the strands will relate or integrate.
10: Quantitative variables and qualitative phenomena/domains use appropriate terminology for their own strand.
The unit(s) represented in each strand are clear.
I have not forced the qualitative strand into IV/DV language.
11: Sampling, collection quality, ethics, and generalization/transferability are considered for both strands.
The two strands have compatible case linkage where integration requires it.
Each measure/procedure supports its intended interpretation.
12: Both strand procedures and data structures are documented.
The integration point is stated before final interpretation.
Missing/exclusion/coding rules are explicit for each evidence type.
13: Quantitative data and qualitative corpus are each quality-checked before integration.
IDs/linkage are preserved when the same cases contribute both strands.
Early summaries do not collapse one evidence type into the other.
14: Each strand uses an analysis appropriate to its evidence type.
The integration method explains how results will be connected, compared, or merged.
Quantitative significance is not used to override contradictory qualitative evidence automatically.
15: Results distinguish quantitative, qualitative, and integrated findings.
Each finding is traceable to its evidence source.
Convergence and divergence between strands are reported.
16: The Discussion explains what the strands jointly add.
Contradictions between strands are analyzed rather than hidden.
Limitations address both strand-specific and integration-specific weaknesses.
